ECharts in RO style

Source: vignettes/echarts-in-ro-style.qmd

This vignette covers the echarts4r functions in ROvis: ro_e_standard() and ro_e_theme(). They let you build interactive charts that follow the Rijksoverheid (RO) visual style. ro_e_standard() is the recommended one: it applies the theme and adds all accessibility features. ro_e_theme() is the styling only. If you are new to echarts4r, we recommend checking out the echarts4r documentation first.

Important

In this vignette, the examples specifically follow the style guidelines of the National Institue for Public Health and the Envrionment (RIVM).

Setup

Load the packages we need:

library(echarts4r)
library(dplyr)
# library(ROvis)
library(ROvis.echarts)
library(ROvis.utils)

We use a small synthetic dataset throughout this vignette so you can run everything standalone:

sex_levels <- c("Women", "Men", "Total")

# Reported cases per age group and sex
dat_cases <- data.frame(
  agegroup = rep(c("0-19", "20-39", "40-59", "60-79", "80+"), times = 3),
  sex = factor(rep(sex_levels, each = 5), levels = sex_levels),
  n = c(
    12000,
    48000,
    61000,
    43000,
    18000,
    10000,
    45000,
    58000,
    39000,
    14000,
    22000,
    93000,
    119000,
    82000,
    32000
  )
)

# Reported cases per week (three series)
dat_weekly <- data.frame(
  week = factor(rep(1:12, times = 3), levels = 1:12),
  sex = factor(rep(sex_levels, each = 12), levels = sex_levels),
  n = c(
    800,
    950,
    1100,
    1400,
    1600,
    1550,
    1300,
    1100,
    900,
    750,
    600,
    500,
    700,
    880,
    1020,
    1300,
    1480,
    1420,
    1180,
    990,
    820,
    680,
    540,
    440,
    1500,
    1830,
    2120,
    2700,
    3080,
    2970,
    2480,
    2090,
    1720,
    1430,
    1140,
    940
  )
)

Apply the RO style

ro_e_standard() applies the RO visual style to any echarts4r chart and adds all accessibility features (see Accessibility features). It slots into an echarts4r pipeline the same way ro_gg_theme() does in ggplot2. Add it at the end, after all your chart layers:

dat_cases |>
  filter(sex == "Women") |>
  e_charts(agegroup) |>
  e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>
  e_title("Cases by age group", "Women only") |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard()

Chart types

Column chart (grouped)

For grouped charts, group the data with dplyr::group_by() before piping into e_charts():

dat_cases |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  e_charts(agegroup) |>
  e_bar(n) |>
  e_title("Cases by age group and sex") |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_con")

Horizontal bar chart

Use e_flip_coords() to turn a column chart into a horizontal bar chart:

dat_cases |>
  filter(sex == "Women") |>
  e_charts(agegroup) |>
  e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>
  e_flip_coords() |>
  e_title("Cases by age group", "Women only") |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Age class") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard()

Line chart 

dat_weekly |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  e_charts(week) |>
  e_line(n) |>
  e_title("Weekly cases by sex") |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Week") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_con")

A note on x-axis variable types: if your x-axis variable is numeric (like a year or week number), echarts4r treats it as a value axis. The RO theme shows grid lines on all value axes, so you will end up with vertical grid lines as well as horizontal ones. To avoid this, make the x-axis variable a factor with explicit levels. That way echarts4r uses a category axis, which has no grid lines, while the order of the values stays correct. For example, we achieved this by:

# Turns week into a category axis without changing the order
week = factor(rep(1:12, times = 3), levels = 1:12)

For convenience, there will also be a warning displayed when you try to do so:

data_multi <- data.frame(
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024),
  women = c(120, 145, 160, 175, 190),
  men = c(95, 110, 125, 140, 150)
)

data_multi |>
  e_charts(year) |>
  e_bar(women, name = "Women") |>
  e_bar(men, name = "Men") |>
  ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_con")
Warning: ! The x-axis variable is numeric, which creates a continuous axis.
ℹ If not intended, convert the variable to a factor: `mutate(year =
  factor(year))`

Grouped trendline 

tab_cases_week_by_prov <- expand.grid(
  week = seq(as.Date("2022-04-01"), by = "week", length.out = 20),
  Province = c("Flevoland", "Groningen", "Noord-Brabant", "Utrecht", "Zeeland")
) |>
  mutate(n = sample(10:1000, n(), replace = TRUE))

tab_cases_week_by_prov |>
  group_by(Province) |>
  e_charts(x = week) |>
  e_line(n) |>
  e_axis_labels(y = "Number of cases") |>
  e_x_axis(
    name = "Date",
    formatter = htmlwidgets::JS(
      'function (value) {
    var monthShortNames = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun",
                           "Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"];
    var d = new Date(value);
    return monthShortNames[d.getMonth()] + "  " + d.getFullYear();
  }'
    )
  ) |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_title("Cases per week for 5 Dutch provinces") |>
  e_legend() |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "item") |>
  ro_e_standard()

Aspect ratio

By default, ro_e_standard() enforces fixed aspect ratios in accordance with the RO data visualisation guidelines: the total element (title + chart + legend) is 2:1 width-to-height, and the inner plot area (grid only, without axis labels or legend) is 3:1 width-to-height. Both ratios update automatically whenever the container width changes, for example when the browser window is resized or a Shiny sidebar is toggled. This is controlled by the fixed_aspect argument, which defaults to TRUE.

dat_cases |>
  filter(sex == "Women") |>
  e_charts(agegroup) |>
  e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>
  e_title("2:1 aspect ratio (default)", "fixed_aspect = TRUE") |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard()

Set fixed_aspect = FALSE when you need to control the chart height yourself, for example inside a Shiny app with a fixed-height container or a dashboard where the chart must fill an exact pixel area. The chart then keeps the height you specify (via e_charts(height = …) or the chunk’s fig.height option) and stops adjusting it on resize:

dat_cases |>
  filter(sex == "Women") |>
  e_charts(agegroup, height = 400) |>
  e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>
  e_title("Fixed 400 px height (fixed_aspect = FALSE)") |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard(fixed_aspect = FALSE)

Color palettes

ro_e_standard() accepts a palette argument. The available palettes are the same ones used by ro_color_palette():

  • "categorical" (default) for general categorical data
  • "gender_con" for conventional gender colors
  • "gender_unc" for unconventional gender colors
  • "full" for all 18 RO colors
  • "greys" for grey tints only

You can preview any palette with ro_show_colors():

ro_show_colors("categorical")
ro_show_colors("gender_con")
ro_show_colors("gender_unc")
ro_show_colors("greys")

Apply a different palette by passing its name to ro_e_standard():

dat_cases |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  e_charts(agegroup) |>
  e_bar(n) |>
  e_title("Cases by age group and sex", "gender_unc palette") |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_unc")

Accessibility features

Interactive charts need to be accessible to keyboard-only users. ro_e_standard() applies ro_e_theme() and adds keyboard and screen reader support on top:

  • Arrow keys move the tooltip across data points. The direction is auto-detected from the chart orientation (left/right for column and line charts, up/down for horizontal bar charts). You can also set it explicitly with axis. The chart needs focus first: Tab to it or click it. Screen readers read out the tooltip content at every step.
  • Tab focuses legend items; Enter or Space toggles them. Screen readers announce each legend item as a button with its on/off state. The legend is part of ro_e_theme(), so this also works with the theme alone.
  • Screen readers announce the chart title first, before the axes and data, and read the axis labels in axis order (left to right, bottom to top). This needs renderer = "svg", the default.

Try it on the line chart: Tab to the chart and use the arrow keys, or Tab further to the legend. ro_e_standard() takes the same styling arguments as ro_e_theme(), plus axis:

dat_weekly |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  e_charts(week) |>
  e_line(n) |>
  e_title(
    "Weekly cases by sex",
    "Use arrow keys to navigate, Tab + Enter/Space to toggle series"
  ) |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Week") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_con")

You can also extend this further. For example, in the case of Dutch provinces:

tab_cases_week_by_prov |>
  group_by(Province) |>
  e_charts(x = week) |>
  e_line(n) |>
  e_axis_labels(y = "Number of cases", x = "Date") |>
  e_x_axis(
    formatter = htmlwidgets::JS(
      'function (value) {
    var monthShortNames = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun",
                           "Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"];
    var d = new Date(value);
    return monthShortNames[d.getMonth()] + "  " + d.getFullYear();
  }'
    )
  ) |>
  e_title("COVID-19 cases per week for 5 Dutch provinces") |>
  e_legend() |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "item") |>
  ro_e_standard(axis = "both")

For a horizontal bar chart, ro_e_standard() auto-detects the vertical orientation and binds the up/down arrow keys instead:

dat_cases |>
  filter(sex == "Women") |>
  e_charts(agegroup) |>
  e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>
  e_flip_coords() |>
  e_title("Cases by age group", "Use up/down arrow keys to navigate") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Age class") |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard()

Styling only

For a chart that ro_e_standard() doesn’t cover, apply only the RO styling with ro_e_theme(). It takes the same styling arguments, but it adds no accessibility features apart from the keyboard-accessible legend, so prefer ro_e_standard() whenever you can.

dat_cases |>
  filter(sex == "Women") |>
  e_charts(agegroup) |>
  e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>
  e_title("Cases by age group", "Styling only") |>
  e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>
  e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_theme()
